edges.description: Retrograde flow can deliver endometrial cells that already harbor cancer-associated mutations to ectopic sites, where they gain a selective advantage and expand clonally.
intermediate_mechanisms: retrograde flow of pre-mutated endometrial cells

edges.description: Cancer-driver mutations confer a selective growth advantage that drives clonal expansion of the epithelial compartment at ectopic sites.
intermediate_mechanisms: selective growth advantage of mutant epithelium

edges.description: Selective expansion of mutated endometrial epithelium at ectopic sites contributes to establishment of endometriosis lesions.
The inflammatory peritoneal microenvironment provides prostaglandin, cytokine, and growth-factor signals that can couple lesion survival to neural and vascular remodeling.
Inflammatory and hormonal mediators from the lesion/peritoneal compartment can lower nociceptor thresholds and amplify pelvic pain signaling.
TGF-beta1 in the inflammatory peritoneal fluid drives peritoneal mesothelial cells toward the glycolytic (Warburg-like) phenotype.

Progesterone resistance prevents progesterone-driven induction of 17beta-HSD-2, so estradiol is not inactivated and local estrogen levels stay high — reinforcing the estrogen-dependent growth of lesions.
Angiogenic lesion programs can coexist with or promote nerve-fiber recruitment in endometriotic implants and adjacent peritoneal tissue.
Lactate secreted by the glycolytic peritoneal microenvironment is implicated in supporting angiogenesis and lesion invasion, coupling the metabolic shift to the angiogenic program.
Newly recruited lesion-associated nerve fibers and neurotrophic factors provide a peripheral substrate that can feed nociceptor sensitization.
Persistent peripheral nociceptive input can contribute to central amplification and broader nociplastic pain processing.
Sensitized pelvic nociceptors amplify the chronic pelvic pain phenotype.
Central amplification can sustain or worsen pelvic pain even when lesion-directed treatment reduces peripheral disease activity.
Multiplexed quantification of MMP and ADAM activities in peritoneal fluid, resolving endometriosis-associated decreases in MMP-2 and ADAM-9 activity.
edges.source: Droplet-based microfluidic protease-activity profiling platform (PrAMA; MIT Griffith/Han)

nodes.description: Investigational non-hormonal anti-angiogenic therapy. The dopamine D2 receptor agonist cabergoline promotes VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) endocytosis, preventing VEGF-VEGFR-2 binding and reducing neoangiogenesis. In experimentally induced endometriosis it decreased the proportion of active lesions and vascularization, and it is being evaluated as a non-hormonal, non-surgical option for endometriosis pain.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine agonist administration causes a reduction in endometrial implants through modulation of angiogenesis in experimentally induced endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: A significant decrease in the percentage of active endometriotic lesions (P < 0.05) and cellular proliferation index (P < 0.001) was found with Cb2 treatment.

nodes.description: Chronic endometriosis-associated pain can involve central nervous system amplification of pain signals and nociplastic pain mechanisms. This downstream state helps explain pain persistence and incomplete response to lesion-directed therapy in some patients.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced pain thresholds and signs of sensitization in women with persistent pelvic pain and suspected endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Our results showed widespread alterations in pain thresholds in women with persistent pelvic pain that are indicative of central sensitization and a time-dependent correlation.

evidence.reference_title: Nociplastic Pain in Endometriosis: A Scoping Review.
evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is an inflammatory chronic condition associated with nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic pain. Central sensitization (CS) is the primary nociplastic pain mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: The Impact of Targeted Endometriosis Treatment On Patients With Central Sensitization: Systematic Review and Meta Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Patients with CSS have smaller changes in pain scores after endometriosis surgery (RR 0.79, confidence interval 0.73-0.86) and significantly higher persistent pain (RR 2.27, confidence interval 1.40-3.68).

evidence.reference_title: Transcranial direct current stimulation to reduce chronic pelvic pain in endometriosis: phase II randomized controlled clinical trial.
evidence.snippet: Significant decreased pain perception in both pain measurements (pressure pain threshold and numerical rating scale score) was found for the active tDCS group compared with the placebo group.

nodes.description: Ectopic lesions trigger chronic pelvic inflammation with elevated cytokines and prostaglandins. Inflammatory milieu contributes to pain and adhesion formation.

evidence.reference_title: Immunology of endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Increased levels of several cytokines and growth factors which are secreted by either immune and endometrial cells seem to promote implantation and growth of ectopic endometrium by inducing proliferation and angiogenesis.

nodes.description: Investigational non-hormonal, non-contraceptive metabolic therapy. The pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK) inhibitor / PDH activator dichloroacetate reverses the aberrant glycolytic phenotype of peritoneal mesothelial cells, reduces lactate secretion, and shrank lesions in a mouse model; a single-arm open-label feasibility trial (EPiC) is evaluating it for endometriosis-associated pain ahead of a planned placebo-controlled trial.

evidence.reference_title: Repurposing dichloroacetate for the treatment of women with endometriosis
evidence.snippet: Oral DCA reduced peritoneal fluid lactate concentrations and endometriosis lesion size in a mouse model.

evidence.reference_title: Dichloroacetate as a possible treatment for endometriosis-associated pain: a single-arm open-label exploratory clinical trial (EPiC).
evidence.snippet: We plan a single-arm, open-label, single site exploratory clinical trial to inform the design of a future randomised controlled trial (RCT) to determine the efficacy of DCA for the treatment of endometriosis-associated pain.

nodes.description: Picoliter-scale droplet-microfluidic platform (barcoded droplet library with pico-injection and Proteolytic Activity Matrix Analysis deconvolution) for multiplexed metalloproteinase activity profiling in small-volume clinical samples, applied to peritoneal fluid from subjects with and without endometriosis. A non-animal New Approach Methodology that resolves specific MMP and ADAM enzymatic activities in cell-free clinical fluid.
nodes.id: Droplet-based microfluidic protease-activity profiling platform (PrAMA; MIT Griffith/Han)

nodes.description: Endometriosis is associated with altered extracellular-matrix metalloproteinase activity in the peritoneal compartment. Multiplexed droplet-microfluidic protease-activity profiling of patient peritoneal fluid — a non-animal, microphysiological (New Approach Methodology) measurement platform — resolved disease-associated differences in specific metalloproteinase activities, in particular decreased MMP-2 and ADAM-9 activity in subjects with endometriosis versus controls. This describes a measured activity signature in the peritoneal microenvironment rather than an established causal driver of lesion establishment.

evidence.reference_title: Multiplexed protease activity assay for low-volume clinical samples using droplet-based microfluidics and its application to endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: The results showed clear and physiologically relevant differences with disease, in particular, decreased MMP-2 and ADAM-9 activities.

experimental_models.description: Multiplexed quantification of MMP and ADAM activities in peritoneal fluid, resolving endometriosis-associated decreases in MMP-2 and ADAM-9 activity.
experimental_models.name: Droplet-based microfluidic protease-activity profiling platform (PrAMA; MIT Griffith/Han)

nodes.description: Endometrial-like tissue grows outside the uterus, commonly on ovaries, fallopian tubes, and pelvic peritoneum. Responds to hormonal cycling with bleeding and inflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Immunology of endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is classically described as the presence of both endometrial glandular and stromal cells outside the uterine cavity, mainly in the pelvis.

nodes.description: Endometrial epithelial cells carrying cancer-associated mutations show rising mutant-allele fractions at ectopic sites relative to normal endometrium, marking clonal selection and expansion of the epithelial compartment. This supports a model in which refluxed, already-mutated cells gain a selective advantage and establish lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Clonal Expansion and Diversification of Cancer-Associated Mutations in Endometriosis and Normal Endometrium.
evidence.snippet: Remarkable increases in MAF of mutations in cancer-associated genes in endometriotic epithelium suggest retrograde flow of endometrial cells already harboring cancer-associated mutations, with selective advantages at ectopic sites, leading to the development of endometriosis.

nodes.description: Endometriotic lesions produce their own estrogen via aromatase and are highly estrogen-responsive. Progesterone resistance impairs normal tissue regression.

evidence.reference_title: Estrogen production in endometriosis and use of aromatase inhibitors to treat endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Estrogen is the most important known factor that stimulates the growth of endometriosis. Estrogen delivery to endometriotic implants was classically viewed to be only via the circulating blood in an endocrine fashion. We recently uncovered an autocrine positive feedback mechanism, which favored the continuous production of estrogen and prostaglandin (PG)E2 in the endometriotic stromal cells.

evidence.reference_title: Estrogen production in endometriosis and use of aromatase inhibitors to treat endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: The enzyme, aromatase, is aberrantly expressed in endometriotic stromal cells and catalyzes the conversion of C19 steroids to estrogens, which then stimulate cyclooxygenase-2 to increase the levels of PGE2. PGE2, in turn, is a potent inducer of aromatase activity in endometriotic stromal cells. Aromatase is not expressed in the eutopic endometrium.

evidence.reference_title: Estrogen production in endometriosis and use of aromatase inhibitors to treat endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: In addition, we find that endometriotic tissue is deficient in 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, which is normally expressed in eutopic endometrial glandular cells and inactivates estradiol-17beta to estrone. This deficiency is another aberration that favors higher levels of estradiol-17beta in endometriotic tissues in comparison with the eutopic endometrium.

nodes.description: Ectopic lesions experience hypoxia which stabilizes HIF-1alpha, upregulating VEGF and promoting angiogenesis. Neovascularization supports lesion survival and growth. Ovarian endometriomas show particularly high expression of hypoxic and angiogenic factors.

evidence.reference_title: Different Expression of Hypoxic and Angiogenic Factors in Human Endometriotic Lesions.
evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is associated with local angiogenic and hypoxic mechanisms. Indeed, peritoneal fluid of women with endometriosis generates a specific microenvironment to support the growth and development of ectopic endometrial tissues.

evidence.reference_title: Different Expression of Hypoxic and Angiogenic Factors in Human Endometriotic Lesions.
evidence.snippet: Ovarian endometrioma expresses high levels of HIF-1/2α, PAR-1/4, and VEGF-A, while DIE did not show significantly different gene expression compared to endometrium from unaffected women. A positive correlation between the expression of HIF-1/2α and VEGF-A mRNA was observed in OMA.

evidence.reference_title: Expression of MMIF, HIF-1α and VEGF in Serum and Endometrial Tissues of Patients with Endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: The results showed that serum concentrations of MMIF, HIF-1α, and VEGF were significantly higher in EM patients than in controls (P<0.05). The expression of all three proteins in both serum and endometrial tissues increased significantly with the R-AFS stage (P<0.05) and with dysmenorrheal severity (P<0.05).

nodes.description: Endometriotic lesions and peritoneal fluid can acquire neuroangiogenic properties, including nerve-fiber growth, altered sensory/autonomic fiber distribution, neurotrophin up-regulation, and vascular remodeling. This provides a peripheral anatomic substrate for pain but does not by itself explain perceived pain severity in all patients.

evidence.reference_title: Peripheral changes in endometriosis-associated pain.
evidence.snippet: Endometriotic lesions and peritoneal fluid from women with endometriosis had pronounced neuroangiogenic properties with increased expression of new nerve fibres, a shift in the distribution of sensory and autonomic fibres in some locations, and up-regulation of several neurotrophins.

evidence.reference_title: Endometriosis: the role of neuroangiogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Recent evidence indicates that ectopic endometriotic implants recruit their own unique neural and vascular supplies through neuroangiogenesis.

nodes.description: Chronic pelvic pain is a cardinal symptomatic burden of endometriosis and may be cyclical, non-cyclical, or persistent after lesion-directed therapy when sensitization mechanisms are established.

evidence.reference_title: Peripheral changes in endometriosis-associated pain.
evidence.snippet: Pain remains the cardinal symptom of endometriosis.

evidence.reference_title: Endometriosis: Classification, pathophysiology, and treatment options.
evidence.snippet: Endometriosis is usually classified into four stages: minimal, mild, moderate, and severe, though it is important to note that the presentation of symptoms does not necessarily correspond to the disease progression.

nodes.description: Lesion and peritoneal mediators, including inflammatory mediators and prolactin/prolactin-receptor signaling, can sensitize pelvic nociceptive sensory neurons. This provides a mechanism by which pain may be amplified without requiring proportional increases in lesion burden.

evidence.reference_title: Prolactin and pain of endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: We highlight our current understanding of prolactin-mediated mechanisms of nociceptor sensitization in females and how this mechanism may apply to endometriosis.

evidence.reference_title: Prolactin and pain of endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: The results of this search strongly indicate that serum prolactin levels are increased in patients with endometriosis and support the possibility that high levels of prolactin may promote pelvic pain in these patients and increase vulnerability to other comorbid pain conditions likely by dysregulating prolactin receptor expression.

evidence.reference_title: Role of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor in Endometriosis Pain.
evidence.snippet: As a result, BDNF concentrations in serum and PF were significantly higher in women with endometriosis with pain (2284.3 ± 51.5 pg/mL, n = 23; 58.8 ± 6.4 pg/mL, n = 16) than in women with endometriosis without pain (1999.8 ± 61.1 pg/mL, n = 37; 31.7 ± 2.9 pg/mL, n = 25; P < .01).

nodes.description: Endometriotic tissue is resistant to progesterone action. Progesterone receptor levels are reduced and the PR-B isoform is essentially absent, so progesterone fails to induce epithelial 17beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (17beta-HSD-2). Because 17beta-HSD-2 normally inactivates estradiol to estrone, its deficient induction leaves high local concentrations of the mitogen estradiol, and this progesterone resistance explains why a subset of patients do not respond to progestin therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Progesterone resistance in endometriosis: link to failure to metabolize estradiol.
evidence.snippet: These in vivo observations are indicative of resistance to progesterone action in endometriosis.

evidence.reference_title: Progesterone resistance in endometriosis: link to failure to metabolize estradiol.
evidence.snippet: The molecular basis of progesterone resistance in endometriosis may be related to an overall reduction in the levels of progesterone receptors (PRs) and the lack of the PR isoform named progesterone receptor B (PR-B).

evidence.reference_title: Progesterone resistance in endometriosis: link to failure to metabolize estradiol.
evidence.snippet: The end result is deficient metabolism of E2 in endometriosis giving rise to high local concentrations of this local mitogen.

nodes.description: Menstrual blood flows backward through fallopian tubes into pelvic cavity. Most women have retrograde menstruation, but only some develop endometriosis, suggesting other factors involved.

evidence.reference_title: Immunology of endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Although multiple theories have been put forth to explain the pathophysiology and pathogenesis of endometriosis, the retrograde menstruation theory of Sampson is the most widely accepted. However, since retrograde menstruation occurs in most of the reproductive age women, it is clear that there must be other factors which may contribute to the implantation of endometrial cells and their subsequent development into endometriotic disease.

nodes.description: Deep-infiltrating endometriotic lesions harbor recurrent somatic cancer-driver mutations (KRAS, PIK3CA, ARID1A, PPP2R1A) that are largely confined to the epithelial compartment. Endometrial cells can already carry these cancer-associated mutations before reaching ectopic sites. Despite these oncogenic drivers, deep-infiltrating lesions remain benign — morphologically normal, non-expansile, and at virtually no risk of malignant transformation; ovarian endometrioma, in contrast, is a recognized precursor of endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Associated Mutations in Endometriosis without Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Five patients harbored known cancer driver mutations in ARID1A, PIK3CA, KRAS, or PPP2R1A, which were validated by Safe-Sequencing System or immunohistochemical analysis.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-Associated Mutations in Endometriosis without Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Ten of 39 deep infiltrating lesions (26%) carried driver mutations; all the tested somatic mutations appeared to be confined to the epithelial compartment of endometriotic lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of heterozygosity on 10q23.3 and mutation of the tumor suppressor gene PTEN in benign endometrial cyst of the ovary: possible sequence progression from benign endometrial cyst to endometrioid carcinoma and clear cell carcinoma of the ovary.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that inactivation of the PTEN tumor suppressor gene is an early event in the development of ovarian endometrioid carcinoma and clear cell carcinoma of the ovary.

nodes.description: Endometriotic lesions and the peritoneal mesothelium of women with endometriosis undergo a cancer-like ("Warburg") metabolic shift away from mitochondrial respiration toward aerobic glycolysis. TGF-beta1, which is elevated in endometriosis peritoneal fluid, drives human peritoneal mesothelial cells to upregulate glycolysis-associated genes (HIF1A, PDK1, LDHA, SLC2A1) and secrete lactate. This glycolytic phenotype — higher glycolysis, lower mitochondrial respiration, and reduced pyruvate dehydrogenase activity — favors lesion establishment and survival and is the target of the investigational metabolic therapy dichloroacetate.

evidence.reference_title: Transforming growth factor-β induced Warburg-like metabolic reprogramming may underpin the development of peritoneal endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Endometriosis lesions expressed higher levels of glycolysis-associated genes HIF1A, PDK1, and LDHA than eutopic endometrium, and adjacent peritoneum had higher levels of HIF1A and SLC2A1 than peritoneum from women without disease

evidence.reference_title: Transforming growth factor-β induced Warburg-like metabolic reprogramming may underpin the development of peritoneal endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Concentrations of lactate in peritoneal fluid paralleled those of TGF-β1, being significantly higher in women with endometriosis compared to women without

evidence.reference_title: Transforming growth factor-β induced Warburg-like metabolic reprogramming may underpin the development of peritoneal endometriosis.
evidence.snippet: Exposure of mesothelial cells to TGF-β1 increased production of lactate (P < .05), increased HIF1A mRNA (P < .05), and protein, and increased concentrations of mRNAs encoded by glycolysis-associated genes (LDHA, PDK1, SLC2A1; P < .05).

evidence.reference_title: Repurposing dichloroacetate for the treatment of women with endometriosis
evidence.snippet: human peritoneal mesothelial cells (HPMCs) recovered from the pelvic peritoneum of women with endometriosis exhibit significantly higher glycolysis, lower mitochondrial respiration, decreased enzymatic activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), and increased production of lactate compared to HPMCs from women without disease
